artifacts.description: feat(kernel): write and read a shape as OCCT BRep text

acceptance_criteria: Two new `Kernel` trait methods, documented: `fn write_brep(&self, s: &Self::Shape) -> Result<String, KernelError>` and `fn read_brep(&self, text: &str) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, implemented for `OcctKernel` through the C ABI shim (`BRepTools::Write` to a string stream, `BRepTools::Read` with a `BRep_Builder` from one). Shim functions are `noexcept` and catch all C++ exceptions; any new `unsafe` stays in `swx-kernel::ffi` with a comment per block.
The text is written without triangulation, so tessellating a shape first does not change its text. Lengths stay in millimetres.
Writing the same shape twice gives identical text, and writing, reading and writing again gives identical text.

Round trip (with `--features occt`), for each of: a 10 × 20 × 30 mm box; a cylinder of radius 5 mm and height 10 mm; and the box with that cylinder cut out of it (cylinder axis along z at x = 5, y = 10, so it goes through the box): the read shape's volume and surface area match the original's within a relative 1e-9, its bounding box matches within 1e-9 mm per coordinate, and its face count is equal. The box's volume is 6000 mm³ within 1e-9 relative.
Bad input gives a `KernelError` and no panic: an empty string, the text `not a brep`, and a valid text cut off halfway.
All existing tests pass unchanged; no test is weakened, removed or ignored.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and CI's `swx-kernel (occt)` job passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
